title: Great Book Chapter 78 — Cosmic Potato / Large-Scale-Structure Morphology Audit
status: book-derived astronomy/cosmology archaeology + quantitative morphology/model-selection programme
source: The Great Book Of Potato2.odt, Chapter 78, parsed pages 540-543
abstract: The Cosmic Potato hypothesis is scientifically meaningful only as a predeclared morphology/model-selection problem. The Great Book visually combines Laniakea, Perseus-Pisces and other large-scale structures into rounded or oblong forms and proposes recurring potato-like morphology across scales. Modern large-scale structure, however, is represented by point processes, density/velocity fields, walls, filaments, nodes and attraction basins rather than sharply bounded solid objects. The rigorous question is therefore whether a specified three-dimensional structure is better described by a compact irregular ellipsoid/tuber model than by filament, wall, skeleton or generic ellipsoid baselines when all models are fitted to the same data and selection function. Principal-axis ratios, Minkowski functionals, shapefinders, topology and surface roughness can supply dimensionless descriptors, while simulations provide null distributions. A cross-scale universality claim would require a common statistic or scaling relation measured independently in biological and astronomical systems, not visual similarity. This programme is T2 as a morphology-testing framework; no current result establishes a universal potato shape, and some named targets such as Perseus-Pisces are expected a priori to be strongly filamentary.
historical_thesis: The chapter visually combines Laniakea, Perseus-Pisces and other cosmic-web structures into rounded/oblong 'potato' forms and proposes recurring potato-like morphology across cosmic, biological and quantum scales.
research_question: For a structure defined by an explicit 3D dataset and segmentation rule, does a preregistered tuber-like morphology model outperform filamentary, ellipsoidal and randomized/simulation baselines after accounting for projection, selection effects and model complexity?
maturity: T2 quantitative morphology hypothesis; no universal-shape result established

laniakea.book_use: Our home supercluster and one half of an overlapping cosmic-potato picture.
laniakea.modern_status: The 2014 Laniakea definition is a basin-of-attraction construction from peculiar-velocity flows, roughly 160 Mpc across in that analysis. It is not a sharply bounded solid object. Newer Cosmicflows-4 reconstruction gives some probability to the Laniakea region belonging to a larger Shapley basin.
laniakea.consequence: Shape is dataset, flow-reconstruction, threshold and scale dependent.

perseus_pisces.book_claim: Described as a filamentary structure stretching across billions of light-years and visually overlapping Laniakea into an oval/potato.
perseus_pisces.correction: Modern catalogues treat Perseus-Pisces as a prominent filamentary/branched supercluster complex on scales of tens to more than one hundred Mpc depending definition/tracer, not a simple billion-light-year oval.
perseus_pisces.consequence: Its natural baseline is a filament/skeleton model, not a tuber or ellipsoid.

overlap_claim.audit: The book's two-overlapping-ovals picture is a project visualization rather than a standard astronomical result. It must be reconstructed from actual 3D positions/velocity fields before shape claims are made.

energy_dimensions.book_use: Gravitational flow/dark-matter density are called 'energy dimensions'.
energy_dimensions.correction: Density, velocity, gravitational potential and energy are fields/observables on spacetime, not extra coordinate dimensions. Feature dimension and spacetime dimension must remain separate.

subatomic_shape.book_use: Particles/fields are suggested to share spherical or oblong potato-like forms.
subatomic_shape.correction: Elementary particles are not generally solid geometric blobs. Spatial probability densities or field configurations depend on state, symmetry, interaction and observable. Cross-scale resemblance requires invariant descriptors, not iconography.

data_definition_contract.rule: Do not quote a shape until the object definition is frozen; changing the threshold or tracer population can change topology and axis ratios.

principal_axis_model.semi_axis_proxies: a proportional to sqrt(lambda_1), b proportional to sqrt(lambda_2), c proportional to sqrt(lambda_3)
principal_axis_model.orientation: Eigenvectors define principal directions; bootstrap or posterior resampling should quantify uncertainty.
principal_axis_model.limitation: Covariance axes summarize second moments and can hide branches, holes and multimodality.

minkowski_and_shapefinder_program.minkowski_functionals: For thresholded 3D regions measure volume V, surface area S, integrated mean curvature C and Euler characteristic chi.
minkowski_and_shapefinder_program.one_shapefinder_convention: T=3V/S; B=S/C; L=C/(4 pi); planarity P=(B-T)/(B+T); filamentarity F=(L-B)/(L+B)
minkowski_and_shapefinder_program.convention_warning: Normalizations vary in the literature; freeze the definition before comparing datasets.
minkowski_and_shapefinder_program.roughness_extension: Add a scale-normalized boundary roughness statistic, for example excess area relative to the best-fit ellipsoid at matched volume, with smoothing scale declared.
minkowski_and_shapefinder_program.topology: Euler characteristic/Betti numbers can distinguish a compact lumpy body from a multiply connected network even when both project to an oval.

potato_hypothesis_pre_registration.example_definition: H_P: a connected 3D region whose best-fit shape is compact/triaxial with moderate axis asymmetry, low-to-moderate filamentarity, bounded planarity and positive nonzero roughness above the instrumental/smoothing floor.
potato_hypothesis_pre_registration.important_rule: Numerical cutoffs for q,s,P,F and roughness must be fixed from an independent training/reference set or physical definition before testing the named cosmic target.
alternative_models: simulation halo/supercluster shapes from the same segmentation algorithm
potato_hypothesis_pre_registration.model_selection: Use held-out likelihood, cross-validation, information criteria or simulation-based classification rather than choosing the model that looks most potato-like after inspection.

projection_and_selection_tests.rotation_test: Measure descriptor stability over 3D rotations and realistic lines of sight. A 2D potato appearance that disappears in 3D is not evidence for a tuber morphology.
projection_and_selection_tests.mask_test: Apply the survey mask/selection function to mocks and quantify induced changes in q,s,P,F and topology.
projection_and_selection_tests.smoothing_test: Repeat over a preregistered physically reasonable range of smoothing scales; report which conclusions are robust and which are scale-specific.
projection_and_selection_tests.uncertainty: Bootstrap tracers or propagate posterior velocity/distance uncertainties rather than treating a reconstructed boundary as exact.

cross_scale_universality_contract.requirement: A genuine universal Potato morphology claim needs a dimensionless descriptor vector Z=(q,s,P,F,roughness,topology,...) defined comparably across systems.
cross_scale_universality_contract.test: Fit a hierarchical distribution p(Z|class,scale) and ask whether a shared scale-invariant family explains independently sampled biological and cosmic objects better than separate families.
cross_scale_universality_contract.stronger_requirement: A common scaling exponent or generative mechanism is much stronger evidence than overlapping visual descriptor ranges.
cross_scale_universality_contract.failure: If descriptor distributions shift substantially by scale/object class or a generic ellipsoid/filament mixture explains both, the universal morphology claim is unsupported.

null_models: randomized point cloud preserving radial/selection function
structures extracted from cosmological simulations using the same pipeline
modern_data_targets: Cosmicflows peculiar-velocity reconstructions for attraction-basin morphology
CLASSIX or comparable cluster catalogues for Perseus-Pisces membership/shape
public galaxy redshift catalogues for 3D point-cloud/skeleton comparison
cosmological simulations for null distributions of shape descriptors
falsification_and_failure_conditions: Filament/skeleton or generic ellipsoid models outperform the preregistered tuber model on held-out/simulation-calibrated criteria.
The tuber classification is unstable to reasonable reconstruction, threshold, rotation or smoothing choices.
The apparent cross-scale similarity disappears when the same dimensionless descriptors and uncertainty treatment are used.
The potato category can only be defined after inspecting the target, producing an unfalsifiable pattern-recognition loop.
completion_path: Choose one cosmic target and freeze its dataset/segmentation.
Implement the descriptor pipeline and uncertainty propagation.
Generate simulation/null distributions using the identical pipeline.
Predefine the tuber-class rule from independent data or morphology theory.
Only after a robust single-scale result test cross-scale universality.
e8_neighbor_correction: Chapter 82 immediately following Chapter 78 calls E8 '248 dimensions'. Existing repository audits correctly repair this: 248 is the dimension of the E8 Lie algebra/adjoint representation, while E8 has rank 8; it is not 248 ordinary spacetime dimensions.
